authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8056.1 pāda lists Prakrit pāya, Hindi pā/pā̃u “foot, leg”, Old Marwari pāya/pāva and Marathi/Gujarati pāy. It discusses final u/v as incorporation of inflectional endings, with pādu an explicitly less probable alternative; that qualification is retained. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11616 viṃśati explicitly gives Kalasha bīši, Maiya bīš, Awan vī and Western Pahari bī in the addendum, alongside eastern bis. This supports the survey twenty forms, including northern loss of the final sibilant. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9691 ma explains replacement of the first-person nominative by oblique/instrumental forms: Prakrit maē, Apabhramsha maĩ, Hindi/Punjabi maĩ, Western Pahari me/mu, Marathi mī, and Oriya mu. It explicitly lists Chilis/Gowro ma. These survey first-person forms select ma, not aham or asme. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open.
